verdict: Linde posted record sales of $9.4B, up 9%, but $425M of cost-reduction and other charges cut GAAP profit to $1.7B — excluding them, earnings rose 7%.

kpis.label: Operating cash flow
kpis.note: up 8% YoY; $1.8B of free cash flow after capex

segments.name: Americas
segments.note: Industrial gases across the Americas — the largest business. Underlying sales rose 9% on 6% higher pricing and 3% higher volumes, led by electronics, chemicals & energy and metals & mining.

segments.name: APAC
segments.note: Asia Pacific gases. Underlying sales rose 8% on pricing, volumes, electronics and chemicals & energy demand and project start-ups.

segments.name: EMEA
segments.note: Europe, Middle East & Africa gases. Underlying sales rose 3%, led by healthcare and food & beverage.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.note: Designing and building gas plants for Linde and third parties. Order intake was $499M and the third-party equipment backlog stood at $2.9B.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Everything else, including the U.S. homecare business (moved into this category in 2026) and surface-coating activities.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of gas plants, tanks and equipment over their lives — including purchase-accounting amortization from the Linde AG merger.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling gases and running the company day to day.

opex.name: Cost reduction program & other charges
opex.note: Charges from Linde's cost-reduction program and other items management strips out of its adjusted results — a year ago this line was an $11M credit.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new gas applications and process technology.

opex.name: Other income, net
opex.note: A credit: $27M of other income inside operating profit, so it reduces expenses.

otherDetail: Net expense of $9M: $71M of net interest expense and $48M of profit belonging to noncontrolling partners, partly offset by $61M of income from equity investments and a $49M pension and retiree-benefit credit.
oneTimers: Cost reduction program and other charges were $425M in the quarter. Excluding these charges and Linde AG purchase-accounting effects, adjusted operating profit was $2,763M (up 8%, a 29.4% margin), adjusted net income $2,122M and adjusted EPS $4.59 (up 9%).

takeaways.title: Record sales, broad growth
takeaways.text: Sales hit a record $9,404M, up 9% — underlying sales up 5% on 3% pricing and 2% volumes, with electronics, chemicals & energy and manufacturing leading. Every segment grew.

takeaways.title: Charges hide the underlying trend
takeaways.text: GAAP operating profit fell to $2,150M because of $425M of cost-reduction and other charges. Adjusted operating profit rose 8% to $2,763M and adjusted EPS rose 9% to $4.59 — both records.

takeaways.title: Backlog keeps building
takeaways.text: The project backlog reached $11B, including a $7.9B contractual sale-of-gas backlog. Full-year capex is guided at $5.5–6.0B and adjusted EPS at $17.82–$17.92, up 8–9%.

footerNote: Net income here is the $1,692M attributable to Linde plc shareholders — after $48M belonging to noncontrolling interests — matching the $3.66 EPS. Linde's segment operating profits are adjusted figures (they total $2,763M); the flow uses GAAP operating profit of $2,150M from the Form 10-Q income statement.
